guides.title: Where to take a mattress in Minneapolis
guides.h1: Where to take a mattress in Minneapolis
guides.dek: If you have City of Minneapolis garbage service, the cheapest option is usually curbside pickup on recycling week. If you need to drop one off today, the city’s South Transfer Station or Hennepin County’s Brooklyn Park facility will take it — with fees or a voucher. Bloomington, Eagan, and Blaine will not.

sections.heading: The short answer
paragraphs: Minneapolis treats mattresses and box springs as large recyclable items. What you can do depends on whether you have City garbage collection, only a Minneapolis water bill, or neither.

City collection customers can set out a mattress on recycling week, or use a pre-requested voucher at the South Transfer Station. Anyone in Hennepin County can also pay $25 per piece at the Brooklyn Park drop-off facility. The Bloomington county facility, Dakota County’s Recycling Zone, and Anoka County’s hazardous-waste site do not accept mattresses. Ramsey County’s Environmental Center pages checked on November 20, 2026 do not list mattresses as accepted.

sections.heading: Option 1: Curbside on recycling week (City collection only)
paragraphs: If your carts say “property of the City of Minneapolis,” crews will take mattresses and box springs as large items, but only when they are set out on your recycling week — not on a regular garbage week. The city’s large-item page, last updated November 19, 2026, says:

Put the mattress out by 6 a.m. on your recycling pickup day. Attach a note that says “For Solid Waste.” Keep it as dry as possible. Waterlogged or frozen mattresses are too heavy and will not be collected for recycling.
Crews note these items on recycling day, leave a “We’ll be back” sticker, and return the next business day. Leave the item at the collection point with the sign and sticker on until it is picked up.

If you would rather set the mattress out at 6 a.m. on the actual collection day instead of recycling day, the city says you must call Solid Waste & Recycling on or before your regularly scheduled recycling pickup day, at 612-673-2917.

You may set out up to two large items each week. A mattress and a box spring are two items. If you do not have City collection (for example, you use a private hauler or a dumpster), this curbside option does not apply.
sections.callout: Holiday note, week of November 23, 2026: the city says collection is delayed one day for residents whose regular pickup day is Thursday or Friday that week, and the Solid Waste office is closed Thursday, November 26, 2026. Confirm current delays on the large-item page before you set anything out.

sections.heading: Option 2: Minneapolis South Transfer Station
paragraphs: The South Transfer Station at 2850 20th Ave S, Minneapolis, MN 55407 accepts mattresses and box springs. Each mattress or box spring counts as one large recyclable item. Hours are Tuesday–Friday, 12:30–7:30 p.m., and Saturday, 8:30 a.m.–3:30 p.m.

You cannot just show up. If you have City garbage service, call 612-673-2917 Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–4:30 p.m., and request a voucher before you go. Vouchers are not issued at the station. City garbage customers get up to six cleanup vouchers a year; each voucher covers up to two large recyclable items (appliances, electronics, or mattresses) and up to 2,000 pounds of garbage or construction debris, for one load in one vehicle.

If you go over the voucher limit, the overage is billed to the property utility account: a $15 administrative fee plus $25 for each extra mattress or box spring. Cash, checks, and credit cards are not accepted at the station.

If you do not have City garbage collection but do have a Minneapolis water bill, you can request a pay-per-use pass. That pass has a $15 administrative fee, a $40 minimum, and $25 per mattress or box spring, also billed to the utility account.
You must have City garbage or water service to use this site. The voucher or pass has to match the property, and the person listed on it must stay on site.

sections.heading: Option 3: Hennepin County Brooklyn Park drop-off
paragraphs: Hennepin County accepts mattresses, futon mattresses, crib mattresses, and box springs from households at one facility only: the Brooklyn Park drop-off at 8100 Jefferson Highway, Brooklyn Park, MN 55445. The fee is $25 per piece. A factory-split box spring counts as two pieces. Cash, check, and major credit or debit cards are accepted.

Hours are Tuesday–Saturday, 9 a.m.–5 p.m. Bring proof of residency, such as a driver’s license or utility bill. This option is for household mattresses, not business, property-manager, or hotel loads.

The county does not accept waterbeds, air mattresses, hospital bed frames, sleeper sofas, or soiled or bedbug-infested mattresses. The Bloomington drop-off at 1400 West 96th Street does not take mattresses.

sections.heading: Places that will not take a mattress
paragraphs: Dakota County’s Recycling Zone in Eagan lists mattresses and box springs as not accepted. Anoka County’s Household Hazardous Waste Facility in Blaine does not accept mattresses (it is a hazardous-waste site, not a transfer station). Ramsey County’s Environmental Center pages reviewed on November 20, 2026 list household hazardous waste, electronics, small appliances, recycling, scrap metal, and similar items — not mattresses. Call Ramsey’s Recycling & Disposal Hotline at 651-633-3279 before assuming otherwise.

sections.heading: If the mattress is still usable
paragraphs: Hennepin County’s Green Disposal Guide says mattresses in good condition can be sold, given away, or donated to Bridging. Ask the store selling you a new mattress whether it will take the old one. The county also points to Second Chance Recycling for pickup in some parts of the county. Confirm current intake rules with those organizations directly; donation sites often reject stained, wet, or bedbug-infested mattresses.

sections.heading: If you cannot haul it yourself
paragraphs: A licensed junk-removal or hauling service can pick the mattress up at the curb. That costs more than a county drop-off or a City voucher, but it is the practical option if you have no vehicle, a third-floor walk-up, or a mattress the official sites will not take (for example, a soiled or infested one — ask the hauler and the city how they want those handled before you set it out).
This directory lists official public drop-off rules first. It does not currently use affiliate links.

guides.title: Where to take leftover paint in Minneapolis
guides.h1: Where to take leftover paint in Minneapolis
guides.dek: Do not take paint to the Minneapolis South Transfer Station — the city lists paint and paint cans as not accepted. Eligible households can drop liquid paint at Hennepin County’s Bloomington or Brooklyn Park facilities, and at several other metro county sites. Minnesota also has a PaintCare program for retailer drop-offs.

sections.heading: The short answer
paragraphs: Leftover household paint in Minneapolis is household hazardous waste, not regular garbage, and not something the city’s South Transfer Station will take. The city’s drop-off page, last updated September 9, 2026, lists “paint or paint cans” under “Do not bring.”

Hennepin County accepts paint, stain, varnish, solvents, and similar materials from Hennepin County households — and household hazardous waste from the other metro counties it lists — at both the Bloomington and Brooklyn Park drop-off facilities, Tuesday–Saturday, 9 a.m.–5 p.m. Five-gallon pails are limited to three per year. Bring proof of residency.

Dakota County’s Recycling Zone in Eagan and Anoka County’s Household Hazardous Waste Facility in Blaine also accept paint from eligible metro residents, with Anoka specifying liquid paint only (dried paint is not accepted there). Ramsey County directs household hazardous waste to the Environmental Center in Roseville; call 651-633-3279 to confirm paint before you drive.

Minnesota participates in PaintCare, which also lists year-round retailer and other drop-off sites. Use PaintCare’s official Minnesota page to find a store; this directory does not copy that retailer list.

sections.heading: Hennepin County drop-off (Bloomington or Brooklyn Park)
paragraphs: Both county facilities accept household paint, stain, varnish, solvents, and driveway sealer. If the paint is in five-gallon pails, Hennepin County limits you to three per year. Containers must be 5 gallons or less, sealed, labeled, kept upright, and carried in a plastic-lined box.

Bloomington: 1400 West 96th Street, Bloomington, MN 55431. Brooklyn Park: 8100 Jefferson Highway, Brooklyn Park, MN 55445. Hours at both: Tuesday–Saturday, 9 a.m.–5 p.m. Phone: 612-348-3777. Email: environment@hennepin.us.

Hennepin County households can use these sites for this material. The county also accepts household hazardous waste from Anoka, Carver, Dakota, Ramsey, Scott, and Washington County households. Sherburne and Wright County residents are not eligible. Business paint is not accepted.
No drop-off charge is listed for ordinary household paint. Stay in your vehicle unless staff says otherwise, and put the cans in the trunk, truck bed, or a trailer.

sections.heading: Other metro county sites
paragraphs: Dakota County Recycling Zone, 3365 Dodd Road (Highway 149), Eagan, MN 55121, lists paint among accepted household hazardous waste and says all accepted items other than TVs, monitors, and tires are free. 2026 hours: Wednesday 9 a.m.–8 p.m., Thursday noon–8 p.m., Friday 9 a.m.–5 p.m., Saturday 8 a.m.–5 p.m. Open to residents of the seven metro counties. Phone: 952-891-7800. Hours change on January 1, 2027.

Anoka County Household Hazardous Waste Facility, 3230 101st Avenue NE, Blaine, MN 55449, accepts “paint (liquid only)” at no charge for eligible residents, and lists dried paint as not accepted. Hours are seasonal: in winter (November–March) Wednesday 1–7 p.m. and Saturday 9 a.m.–3 p.m.; from April–October it adds Thursday, Friday, and Saturday 9 a.m.–3 p.m. Phone: 763-324-3400.

Ramsey County Environmental Center, 1700 Kent Street, Roseville, MN 55113, is the county’s household hazardous waste site and is listed as free for residents of the seven metro counties. The public pages describe accepted hazardous products as those labeled caution, warning, danger, or poison that still contain product. Because those pages do not spell out “latex paint” as a separate line, call the Recycling & Disposal Hotline at 651-633-3279 before a special trip.

sections.heading: Do not take paint here
paragraphs: Minneapolis South Transfer Station does not accept paint or paint cans. Do not put liquid paint in regular household garbage. If a latex can is completely dry, some cities allow it in the trash — Minneapolis and Hennepin rules should be checked on the Green Disposal Guide or with Solid Waste at 612-673-2917 before you assume that.

sections.heading: Retail drop-off through PaintCare
paragraphs: Minnesota has a paint-stewardship program run by PaintCare. The official state page is the right place to look up a retailer, reuse store, or other year-round drop-off, including current limits and what kinds of paint they take. Start at PaintCare’s Minnesota page: https://www.paintcare.org/states/minnesota/
This site does not republish PaintCare’s store list, because those locations and limits change and belong to PaintCare.

sections.heading: Usable leftover paint
paragraphs: Hennepin County and Dakota County both operate reuse shelves (a Free Product Center and a Reuse Zone) where leftover usable paint is sometimes offered to residents for free, with limits. Hennepin noted a temporary closure of the Bloomington Free Product Center beginning May 18 due to construction; confirm whether reuse shelves are open before you go. Do not count on a specific color being in stock.
